::: {#exm-best-constant}

#### Searching for the best constant

For the `mpg` values of the Auto data of @exm-best-constant-auto,
find the constant $c$ that minimizes the average squared error by numerical search, without using the mean:

<!-- no-figure: @fig-best-constant-auto plots the curve this search minimizes -->

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Python

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar

mpg_search = pd.read_csv("data/auto.csv")["mpg"].to_numpy(dtype=float)


def average_squared_error(c):
    """The average squared error of the constant prediction c."""
    return np.mean((mpg_search - c) ** 2)


best_search = minimize_scalar(average_squared_error)
print(best_search.x, best_search.fun)
print(mpg_search.mean(), mpg_search.var())
```

#### R

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
auto_search <- readr::read_csv("data/auto.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
mpg_search <- auto_search$mpg
mpg_range <- range(mpg_search)
# The average squared error of the constant prediction c, minimized over c.
best_search <- optimize(
  \(c) {
    errors <- mpg_search - c
    mean(errors^2)
  },
  interval = mpg_range
)
mean_search <- mean(mpg_search)
deviations_search <- mpg_search - mean_search
variance_search <- mean(deviations_search^2)
c(
  minimizer = best_search$minimum,
  minimum = best_search$objective,
  mean = mean_search,
  variance = variance_search
)
```

:::

The search ends at `{r} sprintf("%.3f", best_search$minimum)`, the mean of `mpg`,
and the smallest error it finds is `{r} sprintf("%.3f", best_search$objective)`, the variance.
This matches @cor-best-constant:
the best constant under squared error is the mean, and the best error is the variance.

:::
